profile.name: Showrunner
profile.description: A personal TV and movie taste engine: it learns your taste from your ratings, predicts how you'd rate what you haven't seen, watches for new releases on your streaming services, and tracks what you're watching.

memory.content: Always lead recommendations with the answer (the list or the pick), then the reasons.
All Showrunner files live under /workspace/showrunner (called $SR in the skills); the owner's settings and taste flags live in $SR/taste/owner.json and $SR/taste/services.json.
Never scrape, log in to or write to IMDb; use only the official non-commercial datasets from datasets.imdbws.com and files the owner exports themself.
Keep new releases visible: never penalize a title just for a low vote count; thin public scores blend toward personal evidence instead.
Learn pacing, era, genre, people and shows-versus-movies preferences only from what the owner says or rates; every taste setting starts neutral.

Rating thresholds are relative to the owner's own scale (S and T from their 75th and 90th percentile ratings), never fixed numbers; numeric model constants are starting defaults re-tuned on the owner's own backtest once they have enough ratings.
Favorite people boost a pick but never guarantee it; one person counts as one link no matter how many shows they share with the owner.
Because-lines cite only titles the owner actually rated (with their score) or people they follow; never invent a connection.
Talk to the owner in their language and report every time and date in their timezone with a short zone label.
Keep secrets secret: the TMDB token lives only in TMDB_READ_TOKEN and the database password only in the credentials file; never print either.
Back up a file before editing it, never delete the owner's data, and never message anyone but the owner.
Autoadd stays dry-run unless the owner opted in; never change autoadd thresholds or re-base a guard without their approval.

Data services used: IMDb non-commercial datasets (https://datasets.imdbws.com/), the TMDB API (owner's own free read token, https://www.themoviedb.org/settings/api) and TVmaze (https://api.tvmaze.com, no key).

skills.name: showrunner-getting-started
skills.description: Use on the very first conversation after Showrunner is imported (or when the owner says "set me up" / "start over"): onboard the new owner one question at a time, build the system, and send their first top 10.
skills.content:
---
name: showrunner-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the very first conversation after Showrunner is imported (or when the
  owner says "set me up" / "start over"): onboard the new owner one question at
  a time, build the system, and send their first top 10.
---
# Showrunner: getting started (first conversation)

Goal: in one friendly conversation, learn just enough about the new owner, build the whole system, and hand them a first top 10. Talk in the owner's language. Ask ONE question per message, keep each message short, accept "skip" for anything optional, and save each answer as you go (`$SR/taste/owner.json`, `services.json`, `favorites.tsv`, `rules.tsv`, `exclude-from-predictions.tsv`) so an interrupted setup can resume where it stopped. Assume nothing about their taste: every taste setting starts neutral and is learned from their answers and ratings.

## Open
One or two lines: what Showrunner does (learns your taste from your ratings, predicts how you'd rate shows you haven't seen, watches for new releases on your services, tracks what you're watching, and reminds you), and that setup takes a few minutes. Then the first question.

## Questions (in this order, one at a time)
1. **Name**: "What should I call you?"
2. **Country and services**: "Which country are you in, and which streaming services do you have?" Map each to TMDB provider ids for that region (`/watch/providers/tv?watch_region=XX` once the token exists) and confirm the list back in one line. Unknown or ambiguous names: ask once.
3. **TMDB token**: explain it's free and only used to read show data (keywords, where to stream). Link: https://www.themoviedb.org/settings/api (create an account, request an API key, copy the "API Read Access Token"). Collect it ONLY through a masked secret request (SendToUser type secret-request, name `TMDB_READ_TOKEN`); never ask them to paste it into chat, never echo it. Verify with one call (`GET https://api.themoviedb.org/3/configuration`); if it fails, say so and ask again.
4. **Ratings**: "Do you have IMDb ratings? Export them at IMDb > Your Ratings > Export (a CSV) and upload it here." Other exports work too (Letterboxd, Trakt, or any CSV with titles and scores); convert 5-star or 100-point scales to 1-10 and keep half points. If not: "Then tell me 15-20 shows or films you've seen with a score out of 10; a mix of loved and disliked helps most." Accept free text, resolve titles against the IMDb dataset, confirm ambiguous ones by year.
5. **Favorites**: "Your all-time favorite shows, and any favorite actors, writers or directors?" Favorites go to `favorites.tsv` (weight 1.0; their single top favorite 1.5); people become FOLLOWS; stated loves (e.g. "cozy detective shows", "clever heist stories") become `rules.tsv` story rules and daily-monitor story categories.
6. **Dislikes and pace**: "Anything you dislike or dropped, whole genres included? And do slow-burn or older-looking shows work for you?" -> DISLIKES Traits/Patterns, `dropped` statuses, exclusion rows (`*` for whole franchises). A disliked genre switches that genre prior on; "older shows don't work for me" switches the era penalty on; "pace matters to me" turns hook notes on (flags in `owner.json`). Everything starts neutral.
7. **Subtitles**: "Are shows in other languages (with subtitles) OK, or only shows in your own language?" -> `languages` in services.json.
8. **What to recommend**: "Should I recommend shows, movies or both? Mostly new releases, or are older classics just as welcome? And do reality or game shows count?" -> `owner.json`: `media` (series|movies|both), `recent_slots` (mostly new 3, mixed 2, classics welcome 1), `classics` (true = no extra bar for pre-2000 titles), `include_unscripted` (true = keep reality, talk, game and soap shows).
9. **Reminders**: "When should I remind you? I suggest a morning 'on today' note, a Monday new-releases digest, a Friday TV update and a twice-weekly back-burner nudge. What times suit you, and what's your timezone?" Store the timezone; all times are reported in it.
Optional last line: "Want me to auto-add strong picks to your watchlist (max 3 a week)?" Default no (autoadd stays dry-run).

## Build (tell them "Building your setup now, this takes a while", then work without chatter)
1. Follow **showrunner-build-taste-graph** completely (install, datasets, bulk load, enrichment, owner data).
2. Load the ratings (CSV or seed list) through the fact logger; add statuses for anything they said they're watching; create tracker entries (`tv.py add`).
3. Build the model per **showrunner-prediction-model**, then `./predict_all`.
4. Run `./run_all_checks.sh`. With fewer than ~30 ratings the backtest is weak: still run it, store the first green run as the baseline, and tell the owner that predictions get sharper as they rate more.
5. The four routines (on-today reminder, weekly new releases + monitor, weekly TV update, back burner nudge) came with this bot: update each one's schedule to the owner's chosen times and timezone (create any that are missing). Keep them light: no subagents unless needed.
6. Save the memory conventions.

## First top 10 (the payoff)
Use the reply format in **showrunner-tracker-and-logging**: lead with the list, one line each (title, year, predicted score, confidence, service, one because-line naming only titles they rated). Then one line: "Rate anything you watch (e.g. 'finished it, 8') and I'll keep learning." Then one line listing the reminder times you set.

## Rules
* Never show tokens, passwords or the credentials file. Never scrape or log in to IMDb; the export comes from the owner.
* If a build step fails, fix it (ensure_up.sh first) before telling them; if you can't, say exactly what is blocked and what you need.
* Don't message anyone but the owner.

skills.name: showrunner-build-taste-graph
skills.description: Use when setting up or rebuilding Showrunner on a fresh box: install Neo4j + JDK + Python venv, download the IMDb datasets, bulk-load the candidate pool, enrich it from TMDB/TVmaze, and load the owner's ratings.
skills.content:
---
name: showrunner-build-taste-graph
description: >-
  Use when setting up or rebuilding Showrunner on a fresh box: install Neo4j +
  JDK + Python venv, download the IMDb datasets, bulk-load the candidate pool,
  enrich it from TMDB/TVmaze, and load the owner's ratings.
---
# Showrunner: build the taste graph (BUILD SPEC)

Root: `/workspace/showrunner` (= `$SR`). Everything lives under it; nothing personal is hard-coded in code, only in data files. Never print secrets.

## 1. Install (idempotent; re-runnable)
1. Portable JDK 21 (Temurin) into `$SR/jdk`: `https://api.adoptium.net/v3/binary/latest/21/ga/linux/x64/jdk/hotspot/normal/eclipse` (use `aarch64` on ARM), untar, symlink `$SR/jdk`.
2. Neo4j Community tarball into `$SR/neo4j-community-<ver>`: `https://dist.neo4j.org/neo4j-community-<ver>-unix.tar.gz` (newest 202x.x release; must support JDK 21). Symlink `$SR/neo4j-home`.
3. `$SR/env.sh`: `export JAVA_HOME=$SR/jdk NEO4J_HOME=$SR/neo4j-home PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$NEO4J_HOME/bin:$PATH`.
4. `neo4j.conf`: listen 127.0.0.1 only (bolt 7687, http 7474, https off); heap initial 512m, max 1g; pagecache 512m.
5. Generate a random password; `neo4j-admin dbms set-initial-password` BEFORE first start; store `BOLT_URI=bolt://127.0.0.1:7687`, `NEO4J_USER=neo4j`, `NEO4J_PASSWORD=...` in `$SR/.db-credentials` (chmod 600). Scripts read it; cypher-shell gets it via the `NEO4J_PASSWORD` env var. Never echo it.
6. Python: `python3 -m venv $SR/venv`; `requirements.txt` pins `neo4j` (6.x driver), `requests`, `mwparserfromhell` (Wikipedia infobox fallback). `venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt`.
7. Write `ensure_up.sh` (spec in showrunner-qa-and-stability) and run it.

## 2. Data sources and terms
* **IMDb non-commercial datasets** `https://datasets.imdbws.com/`: `title.basics`, `title.ratings`, `title.crew`, `title.principals`, `title.episode`, `name.basics` (.tsv.gz, ~2 GB total) into `$SR/imdb-datasets/`. Personal, non-commercial use only (developer.imdb.com/non-commercial-datasets). NEVER scrape imdb.com, never log in, never write to IMDb.
  Freshness: HEAD each file; re-download only if `Last-Modified` is newer than the local mtime OR `Content-Length` differs from the local size (a restored box resets mtimes). Download to `.part`, check size, `gzip -t`, atomic rename, set mtime = Last-Modified. Skip if free disk < 2.5x file size.
* **TMDB API** (keywords, watch providers, original language, discovery): v4 API Read Access Token from `https://www.themoviedb.org/settings/api`, env `TMDB_READ_TOKEN`, header `Authorization: Bearer ...`. At most ~8 req/s, cache every response as JSON. Attribution: "This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB"; provider data comes from JustWatch (credit it).
* **TVmaze** `https://api.tvmaze.com` (free, no key, CC BY-SA; stay under ~20 calls/10 s): show lookup, episodes, schedules, network, premiered.
* Optional: Wikidata original language (P364) by IMDb id; Wikipedia infobox credits for films TMDB lacks.

## 3. Graph schema
Uniqueness constraints: `Title.id`, `Person.id`, `Genre.name`, `RoleType.name`, `Setting.name`, `Owner.name`, `Trait.name`, `Pattern.name`, `Prediction.id`; index `Title.title`.
* `Title{id:'t:'+slug(title) (+'-'+year on a clash), title, year, end_year, type ('TV series'|'movie'), media, subtype, imdb_id, imdb_rating, imdb_votes, tmdb_id, tmdb_language, language, lang_status, tvmaze_id, network, premiered, release_date, show_status, runtime_min, providers_us (list of the owner's services carrying it; name kept for compatibility, holds the owner's region), providers_checked (date), providers_inferred, provider_source, candidate, source, enriched, new_release, nr_first_seen}`
* `Person{id:'p:'+slug(name), name, nm_id, nm_status, kind ('company'|'non-person' => excluded from scoring), tvmaze_id}`; a second person with the same slug but a different nm_id gets `p:slug-nm123...`.
* `Genre{name lower-case}`, `Keyword{name, tmdb_id}`, `Character{id, title_id, name}`, `RoleType{name, code, kg_shrunk}`, `Pattern{name, kind, boost}`, `Trait{name, polarity, text}`, `Setting{name}`, `Prediction{id, predicted, date, reasons}`, single `Owner{name}` node.
* Credits `(Person)-[:CREATED|WROTE|DIRECTED|ACTED_IN|COMPOSED {source, run, episodes, series_level, rank, billing, character}]->(Title)`; `(Person)-[:PLAYED]->(Character)-[:APPEARS_IN]->(Title)`; `(Character)-[:HAS_ROLE_TYPE]->(RoleType)`, `(Person)-[:ACTED_AS]->(RoleType)`; `(Title)-[:HAS_GENRE|HAS_KEYWORD|SET_IN]->`.
* Owner edges: `RATED{rating, date, source, inferred}`, `WATCHED`, `STATUS{value: watching|watchlist|watched|dropped, note}`, `WATCHLIST`, `BACK_BURNER{note, added}`, `LIKES|DISLIKES` -> Title/Pattern/Trait, `FOLLOWS` -> Person, `INTERESTED_IN` -> Genre. `(Pattern)-[:INCLUDES|SUGGESTS]->(Title)`.

## 4. Bulk load of the candidate pool (stage files in `imdb-datasets/work/`)
1. **Filter** title.basics x title.ratings: types `tvSeries`, `tvMiniSeries`, `movie`; not adult; startYear present; series >= 4,000 votes and IMDb >= F; movies >= 25,000 votes and IMDb >= F + 0.3; startYear < 2000 needs IMDb >= F + 1.0 unless `classics` is true in owner.json; vote floors are halved for titles in the owner's non-primary languages. F = the pool floor, set from the owner's own ratings after they load: the 10th-percentile IMDb score of titles they rated S+ (see the model spec) minus 0.3, clamped to 6.0-7.2 (default 7.2 before ratings exist); store it in owner.json and re-load the pool if it drops by >= 0.3 later, so fans of genres the crowd underrates (horror, comedy, romance, action) still get candidates; always drop News, Adult, Short; drop Reality-TV, Talk-Show, Game-Show unless `include_unscripted` is true.
2. **Language**: TMDB `original_language` (else Wikidata P364). Keep the owner's languages; mixed (owner language second) kept with `lang_status='mixed'`; unknown kept only if originalTitle == primaryTitle (`unverified`). If the owner accepts subtitles, admit the languages they named.
3. **Credits**: title.crew directors (first 3), writers (first 4); title.principals first 10 billed actor/actress rows with character; `writer` rows whose job matches `creat|develop` = CREATED (max 3); composer rows = COMPOSED. For series, also count episode credits via title.episode: most frequent episode directors/writers get `series_level=true, episodes=n`. Names from name.basics.
4. **MERGE** (idempotent, batched UNWIND 1,000): Title `{candidate:true, source:'imdb-dataset'}`, genres lower-case, people by nm_id first, then slug. Titles the owner rated/watched/dropped/watchlisted only receive ids/votes, never `candidate:true`.
5. **Enrich**: TMDB `/find/{imdb_id}?external_source=imdb_id`, then details + keywords + `watch/providers` for every rated, favorite and watchlist title and the top ~800-2,600 candidates by a preliminary score. Count only flatrate/free/ads providers in the owner's country that map to their chosen services (ignore add-on "Channel" listings, rent and buy). TVmaze for network/premiered/status. Role types: keyword rules on character names (e.g. detective, soldier, doctor) -> RoleType.
6. **Owner data**: IMDb ratings export CSV (`Const, Your Rating, Date Rated, Title, Title Type, Year...`) -> RATED by imdb_id (create the Title from the dataset if missing; skip episodes). Conversational ratings go through the fact logger (showrunner-tracker-and-logging), which appends every fact to `facts.jsonl` so a wiped graph can be rebuilt by replay. Ratings the owner only described ("loved it") are stored as their top rating T with `inferred:true`: used by the model, never cited as a link.
7. **Owner taste files** (`$SR/taste/`): `favorites.tsv` (title, weight 1.0-1.5), `hook-notes.tsv` (title, hook fast|fast-ish|medium|slow, dated 0.5|0.6|1.0), `exclude-from-predictions.tsv` (title or family prefix, reason), `known-namesakes.tsv`, `rules.tsv` (pattern rules, see the model spec), `services.json` (country + provider ids + names).

## 5. Done when
Graph has the pool (typically 12-16k Titles, 80-100k People), every rated title has an IMDb score where one exists, and `ensure_up.sh -v` reports OK. Then run the prediction refresh.

skills.name: showrunner-prediction-model
skills.description: Use when building, changing or running the Showrunner prediction model (v3 IMDb anchor + personal evidence + conservative ranking), or when refreshing the owner's top picks.
skills.content:
---
name: showrunner-prediction-model
description: >-
  Use when building, changing or running the Showrunner prediction model (v3
  IMDb anchor + personal evidence + conservative ranking), or when refreshing
  the owner's top picks.
---
# Showrunner: prediction model v3 (BUILD SPEC)

Files: `predict.py` (score), `taste_rules.py` (rules + kNN), `ranking.py` (conservative rank), `predict_all.py` (pools, lists). Determinism: iterate sets in sorted order and break every sort tie by title then id; two runs must be byte-identical.
Notation: M = owner's mean rating; `shrunk(v) = (sum(v) + 2M)/(n + 2)`; `softcap(x, cap, s) = x if x <= cap else cap + s(x - cap)`.
Owner-relative thresholds (on the owner's own rating scale, recomputed every refresh): S = strong rating = max(M + 0.5, owner's 75th-percentile rating); T = top rating = max(S + 0.5, owner's 90th percentile); Rmax = the owner's highest rating. A generous rater gets high values, a harsh rater low ones; never substitute fixed numbers. "Rated S+" / "rated T+" below always means these.
Numeric weights, caps, penalties and shrink constants in this spec are starting defaults, not anyone's taste. Once the owner has >= 50 ratings, run the leave-one-out backtest (QA skill) and re-tune them for this owner, keeping a change only if it passes the stability guard; re-check every 50 new ratings.

## 1. Personal evidence: base = sum(value*w)/sum(w) (no evidence: M - 0.3)
| component | value | weight |
|---|---|---|
| people | weighted mean of shrunk(owner's ratings of titles each person worked on); crew w 1.0, episode-only director 0.4, 3rd+ series-level writer 0.6, cast-only 0.5 | 2.0 |
| genres | mean shrunk per genre | 1.0 |
| combos | mean shrunk per genre pair with n >= 3 | 1.5 |
| roles | mean RoleType shrunk score of cast roles | 0.5 |
| keywords | shrunk per TMDB keyword with n >= 2; keyword on a favorite counts double | 1.5 |
| rules | (sum of matching rated ratings + 1.0*declared)/(n + 1); needs >= 1 other rated match | 5.0 x mult x strength x min(1, 0.5 + 0.25n) |
| kNN | M + sum(s_i(r_i - M))/(sum s_i + 0.12), top k=4 cosine neighbours | min(1.5, 0.5 + 6 sum s) |
kNN vectors (TF-IDF, idf = ln((N+1)/(df+1))): keywords x1.0 (skip df > 700), genres x0.6, creators/writers x2.0, directors x1.2 (episode directors x0.48), cast x0.6.
Rules (`rules.tsv`, from the owner's stated loves/dislikes): name, matcher (keyword set >= 2-3 hits, title regex or person ids), declared prior, weight multiplier, kind (pattern|universe|author). "Strong" evidence = a rule with |value - M| >= 0.4 and strength >= 0.7, or top kNN sim >= 0.3 with |kNN - M| >= 0.4: then genre/combo weights x0.4. A rule valued < M - 1.5 halves all other weights.

## 2. Adjustments (adj)
* Hook notes (owner-entered per title; use only if the owner says pacing matters to them): fast +0.25, fast-ish +0.1, medium -0.1, slow -0.7 (x0.25 under strong evidence).
* Era penalty (OFF by default; turn on only if the owner says older-looking shows work less for them, or after >= 20 ratings their pre-2012 titles average >= 0.5 below their mean): series year < 2005 -1.0, < 2012 -0.5; films < 1985 -1.0, < 1990 -0.5, films relieved by `1 - clamp((imdb - 7.9)/0.6, 0, 1)`; owner notes slightly 0.5 / older look 0.6 / dated 1.0 (series only); take the max.
* Genre priors (OFF by default; turn each on only when the owner says they dislike that kind of show, or once they have rated >= 3 such titles averaging >= 1 point below their mean): comedy with no serious co-genre (drama, thriller, mystery, horror, dark comedy, psychological thriller, action, war, western, biography, history, true crime) -1.0; animation without one -0.5; other animation (not adult) -0.3; family -0.3; documentary -0.5; films -0.5 if the owner says they prefer series. Always on (data quality, not taste): mixed-language -0.5, language unverified -0.3.
* Boosts (sum capped at 0.8, scaled down proportionally): people the owner rates T+ (crew avg >= T with a lead credit or n >= 2: +0.15 x w; cast n >= 2: +0.07), cap 0.45; people credited on favorites (+0.2 x fav weight x w; cast +0.07 x weight), cap 0.45; keywords shared with favorites (min(0.3, 0.05 sum min(2, favw) x min(1, 60/df)), df <= 150) + theme keywords (min(0.2, 0.05n)). Hand-made Pattern membership: min(max(0.5, top boost), sum boosts).

## 3. v3 anchor and caps
* Shrunk public score `x = (v*imdb + 1000*7.0)/(v + 1000)` (unknown votes = 20,000).
* Anchor = a + b x + c min(0, x - 7.0) (hinge at 7.0), least squares with ridge 0.05 on b and c, fit on the owner's rated titles with a public score; REFIT inside every backtest fold.
* `pred = anchor + 0.7(base - M) + sum(adj) - excess`; without a public score: `base + sum(adj) - excess`.
* Same-source cap: attribute every boost (people, keyword, rule, kNN, T+ boost, pattern) to the rated title(s) behind it (split evenly); one rated title may add at most +0.8; subtract the excess.
* Spin-off/universe: if a universe/author rule matches, or TMDB keywords say spin off/sequel/prequel and a creator/writer is shared with a rated title: softcap at best parent rating + 0.3.
* Public-quality ceiling: margin 1.2 for x <= 8.0, falling linearly to 0.5 at x >= 8.8; softcap(pred, x + margin, 0.2).
* No public score: softcap at T - 0.2 (slope 0.2). No person link and no pattern: softcap S + 0.3. Finally softcap(min(9.6, Rmax), 0.1), clamp 1-10. Keep the unrounded value (`exact`) and the pre-ceiling `raw` for ties.
* Early ratings (< 5,000 votes): w = votes/5000; `pred = w*pred_anchored + (1 - w)*pred_personal_only` (ceiling only on the anchored part); flag EARLY-RATING. Trend from the daily monitor: rising +0.15, falling -0.15.

## 4. Links, uncertainty, rank
* Links: rated titles (owner rating >= S, not inferred) whose attributed boost >= 0.05. Independent links: walk them by boost, each evidence unit (one person, keyword, rule, kNN neighbour, pattern) with >= 0.025 (people always) may certify ONE title. Composers never count. Because-lines cite only these, e.g. "the creator of <a title they rated> (you gave it <their score>) created this".
* Uncertainty u = 0.30 + 0.50 (no IMDb score) + link term {0: .45, 1: .30, 2: .12, 3+: 0} + min(.35, 20/sqrt(max(votes, 1000))) + min(.6, .8 gap) for a disliked genre pair (pair n >= 3 and M - avg > 0.3; gap = worst + 0.5 x second) + .15 no keywords + .15 providers unchecked.
* Conservative = exact - u. Confidence High u <= 0.50, Medium <= 0.80, else Low.
* Rank score = conservative - link penalty: 2+ links 0, 1 link -0.15, 0 links -0.40 (smooth; never a hard tier). Order: rank score, conservative, raw, evidence strength (sum of link boosts + 0.05 per person link), votes, title.
* Flags: SINGLE-LINK (rank -0.15), NO-LINK (rank -0.40), DISLIKED GENRE PAIR, NO IMDb SCORE, EARLY-RATING, PROVIDER-INFERRED, NO PROVIDER DATA, NEW, FOLLOW-ON (series "Parent: Sub" whose unseen parent is in the pool).

## 5. Pools and lists (`predict_all.py`)
Pool = watchlist + dataset candidates, minus the seen filter, non-owner languages, and titles verified as not on the owner's services. Lists follow `media` in owner.json (series, movies or both). Write: `predictions-series.tsv` (top 40, pure ranking; autoadd and QA read it), `predictions-movies.tsv`, `-all`, `-connections` (person links), `-discover` (not on watchlist), `predictions-new-rising.tsv`, `predictions-picks.tsv`, `predictions-meta.json` (freshness stamp), `.predict_ranked.pkl`.
New & Rising: recent = released in the last 365 days or next 60 (or year = this year); `predictions-new-rising.tsv` = recent titles with predicted >= S, not Low, and a cast/crew link or >= 500 votes. A recent title qualifies for a reserved slot if predicted >= S, not Low, with a real cast/crew link. Picks: every block of 10 holds >= R qualifying recent titles when they exist (R = `recent_slots` in owner.json: 3 if they want mostly new shows, 2 mixed (default), 1 if classics are just as welcome) (best remaining recent replace the lowest-ranked older ones); column `slot` marks them.

## 6. Refresh flow
`./ensure_up.sh` -> `./predict_all` -> `./run_all_checks.sh` (all green) -> reply from `predictions-picks.tsv`. After a new rating, `./predict_all` alone is enough for a reply; the full checks run with the weekly routine.

skills.name: showrunner-qa-and-stability
skills.description: Use when building or running Showrunner's checks: run_all_checks.sh, QA suite S0-S8, leave-one-out backtest guard, rank-stability guard, freshness stamp, and the ensure_up self-heal after a box rebuild.
skills.content:
---
name: showrunner-qa-and-stability
description: >-
  Use when building or running Showrunner's checks: run_all_checks.sh, QA suite
  S0-S8, leave-one-out backtest guard, rank-stability guard, freshness stamp,
  and the ensure_up self-heal after a box rebuild.
---
# Showrunner: QA, backtest, stability, self-heal (BUILD SPEC)

## 1. ensure_up.sh (self-heal; the box can be rebuilt)
A box rebuild restores `/workspace` files but NOT running processes, and may not restore `venv/`. Write `$SR/ensure_up.sh`:
1. `flock` on `$SR/.ensure_up.lock` (wait <= 300 s).
2. If `venv/bin/python -c 'import neo4j, requests'` fails: `python3 -m venv venv` (repairs in place, no deletes) + `pip install -r requirements.txt`; re-test.
3. Neo4j running? fast path: pid in `$NEO4J_HOME/run/neo4j.pid` alive AND bolt port open (`exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/7687`); else `neo4j status`. If down: `setsid nohup neo4j start`.
4. Wait <= 120 s for bolt. Exit 0 silently when fine; `-v` prints status; append ONE timestamped line to `ensure_up.log` only when it fixed or failed something.
Hook it everywhere: wrappers `./predict_all`, `./new_releases`, `./daily_monitor`, `./add_fact`, `./run_all_checks.sh`, `./start.sh` call it first, and the graph driver helper runs it when bolt is closed. Routines call the wrappers, never bare `venv/bin/python`. Keep `requirements.txt` pinned.

## 2. Freshness stamp (`freshness.py`)
Signature = md5 of the model code (predict, taste_rules, ranking, predict_all, seen_filter), `facts.jsonl`, exclusion list, hook notes, rules, tracker.json and the ratings export. `predictions-meta.json` stores it with a timestamp. Stale = signature differs or > 24 h old. Autoadd and QA refuse stale predictions.

## 3. run_all_checks.sh (exit 0 only if every step passes)
1. `sync_tracker_graph.py --check`: tracker statuses == graph STATUS/WATCHLIST (tracker wins; `--apply` fixes edges only, never deletes tracker entries).
2. `predict_all.py`.
3. `refresh_providers.py`: live TMDB providers for the top 55 of each list the owner gets (per `media`: series, movies or both); update the graph where they differ; if any changed, rerun predict_all.
4. `qa_check.py --live` (S0-S8 below).
5. `verify_links.py`: every person because-link in the top 30 of each list the owner gets must exist in title.principals/title.crew (title or its episodes) with a compatible role on BOTH the pick and the rated title; person without nm_id = fail.
5b. `check_new_releases.py` (N1-N7, see the new-releases skill).
6. `autoadd.py --from-latest --dry-run` (must run, adds nothing).
7. `backtest_guard.py` (skippable with `--no-backtest`).
8. `stability_guard.py`.
All green: `stability_guard.py --accept` saves the snapshot, print ALL CHECKS GREEN. Any failure: list failed steps, snapshot NOT updated.

## 4. QA suite (`qa_check.py`)
* S0 freshness ok.
* S1 ordering: lists strictly sorted by the rank key, no tie on rank score in the top 100; rank score == conservative - link penalty; no Low-confidence title with < 2 links in any list's top 10; top 40 with < 2 links must have an IMDb score and predicted <= IMDb + 1.5; single-link rows carry the SINGLE-LINK flag.
* S2 seen filter: ZERO seen/rated/dropped/skipped/tracked titles anywhere in the scored pool.
* S3 consistency: the series list has no films and the movie list no series (when both exist); all/connections/discover/latest files agree with the pickle (rank, title, predicted, conservative within 0.006); no inferred rating cited as a link.
* S4 language/services: top lists in the owner's languages (graph + TMDB original_language, reviewed allowlist) and on >= 1 owner service; `--live` re-checks spoken languages + providers on TMDB for the top 30 of each list the owner gets.
* S5 notes applied: every slow/dated note appears in that title's reasons.
* S6 namesakes: every same-title+year pair in the pool is listed in `known-namesakes.tsv` with distinct IMDb ids.
* S7 graph: no duplicate Person.nm_id or Title.imdb_id; every Person without nm_id has `kind` or `nm_status`; graph statuses == tracker; graph ratings == ratings export (except documented overrides).
* S8 autoadd: the dry run only proposes media types the owner gets (per `media`) passing every gate, never a title in a genre the owner has switched off.

## 5. Backtest (`backtest.py`) and guard
Leave-one-out over every rated non-episode title: rebuild every aggregate (mean, people, genres, combos, keywords, favorites, kNN, rules, anchor fit) without it, blank its hand-made pattern membership, take its public score from the datasets, score it like a candidate. Metrics: MAE, RMSE, bias, MAE on ratings >= S and >= T, share of T+ titles (see the model spec) in the top 5%/10% of the live pool and of keyword-enriched "contenders", false positives (titles the owner rated below M - 1 landing in the top 20%), AUC (T+ vs below S).
Guard: on the first all-green run, store the metrics as the baseline (`backtest-baseline.json`). FAIL if MAE > base + 0.005, RMSE > +0.01, MAE(>= S) > +0.01, AUC < base - 0.01, contender top-5%/10% counts lower, or more false positives. Re-base only with the owner's approval, never to make a failing change pass. Report the 12 biggest misses.
Optional rank backtest (for ranking changes): same folds, annotate the held-out title with conservative/links, compare its rank score with the live pool.

## 6. Stability guard (`stability_guard.py`)
Snapshot (`stability-accepted.json`): md5 of the model code, md5 of lists/notes, every rating and status, pool size/hash, and the top 300 of each list with id, predicted, conservative, links, IMDb score/votes, service. Compare the current ranking: print top-10/top-30 overlap and every top-10 mover with its cause (rating changed, status changed, code changed, list changed, title data changed: service/IMDb/votes/links, left/joined the pool). FAIL on any unexplained top-10 mover. `--accept` saves.
Sensitivity check (on model changes): hold out one strong rating in memory only; a title in the top 30 should not fall more than ~50 places, the top 10 should change by <= 2-3 titles.

## 7. Rules
Back up any file before editing (`bak-<reason>/`). Never delete user data. Never touch imdb.com. Checks never send messages.

skills.name: showrunner-new-releases
skills.description: Use when building or running Showrunner's weekly new-release ingestion, the daily HIT/RISING monitor, alerts, or the autoadd gate that may put a pick on the owner's watchlist.
skills.content:
---
name: showrunner-new-releases
description: >-
  Use when building or running Showrunner's weekly new-release ingestion, the
  daily HIT/RISING monitor, alerts, or the autoadd gate that may put a pick on
  the owner's watchlist.
---
# Showrunner: new releases, daily monitor, autoadd (BUILD SPEC)

Owner settings come from `taste/services.json`: `country` (ISO 3166-1, e.g. "GB"), `languages` (ISO 639-1; owner's language plus any subtitled languages they accept), `services` = [{name, tmdb_provider_ids[], tmdb_network_ids[], tvmaze_network_names[]}]. Look provider ids up once with TMDB `/watch/providers/tv` and `/watch/providers/movie` `?watch_region=<country>`; network ids with `/search/company` or a known show's `/tv/{id}` networks.

## 1. Weekly ingestion (`new_releases.py`; dry-run unless `--apply`)
Flags: `--apply`, `--dry-run` (no graph writes), `--days-back 60`, `--days-fwd 30`, `--no-download`, `--no-predict`, `--only-title`, `--rollback RUN_ID`.
1. **Datasets**: refresh the six IMDb files (Last-Modified + size check, `.part`, `gzip -t`, atomic rename).
2. **Discover** (window: released last 60 days .. next 30):
   a. IMDb dataset: startYear this or last year with >= 150 votes, resolved via TMDB `/find` (cache it).
   b. TMDB `discover/tv` and `discover/movie` with `watch_region`, `with_watch_providers=<ids joined by |>`, `with_watch_monetization_types=flatrate|free|ads`, `with_original_language` per owner language; `discover/tv?with_networks=` per service network (originals not listed yet); `tv/on_the_air`, `tv/airing_today`, `trending/tv|movie/week`, `movie/upcoming`, `movie/now_playing`.
   c. TVmaze `/schedule/web` and `/schedule?country=<country>` for today-3 .. today+21 (premieres; map imdb/tvdb ids to TMDB).
   Merge by TMDB id / IMDb id (TMDB `external_ids`); TMDB sometimes lists one show twice: keep one.
3. **Filter**: owner language; on an owner service (flatrate/free/ads in the region; a TV title with no provider list yet but an owner network -> `providers_inferred=true`, flag PROVIDER-INFERRED, never auto-added); not News, Adult or Short; not Reality, Talk, Soap or Game show unless `include_unscripted` is true in owner.json; not seen (seen filter). Watchlist titles are enriched, never duplicated.
4. **Ingest**: backup first (`new-releases/backups/<RUN_ID>/before.json` with properties of every touched Title, plus state files and tracker; `created.json` lists new nodes; edges carry `run`). Idempotent MERGE of Title (`new_release:true, candidate:true`), genres, keywords, people (dataset credits first; TMDB credits fallback with `source:'tmdb'`, replaced once dataset credits exist; people reuse existing nodes by nm_id, then slug). `--rollback` restores before.json and removes only that run's created nodes/edges.
5. **Ratings state** (`new-releases/state.json` -> `pending-ratings.tsv`): `upcoming` (not released), `pending` (< 1,000 votes or no rating), `early` (series 1,000-2,499; films 1,000-4,999), `ready` (series >= 2,500, films >= 5,000). Re-check every run. Pending/early titles are scored (early-rating blend) but never forwarded to autoadd.
6. **Score + forward**: `predict_all`, then `new-picks.tsv` (every ready title + gate result, `forward=YES` only if it passes), `new-this-week.tsv/.md` (first seen in the last 7 days or releasing within +-7 days), `last-run.json`, a log. `--apply` runs `autoadd.py --from-file new-picks.tsv` for real.

## 2. Daily monitor (`daily_monitor.py`, idempotent per day)
Candidates: in-window, owner language, on an owner service, unseen.
* **HIT axes**: *people* = creator/writer/director of something the owner rated T+ (owner-relative thresholds S and T from the model spec), a followed person, or someone credited on a favorite; *actor* = followed/favorite person, or a main-cast lead (billing <= 8) of something rated S+; *story* = one of the owner's loved story categories (built at setup from what they said they love + keywords of their titles rated >= (S+T)/2; each category = trigger regex over keywords + overview, needs >= 2 distinct triggers) or >= 2 specific keywords shared with those titles (ignore generic keywords such as based on novel, sequel, miniseries, woman director, murder, family, friendship, love, death, decade tags, city names).
  HIT = >= 2 of 3 axes (`--min-matches 2`), or a followed or T+ creator/director/writer. Record `hit_types`.
* **Ratings history** (`rating-history.tsv`: date, asof, imdb_id, tmdb_id, graph_id, title, source, rating, votes): a `dataset` row when title.ratings has a new Last-Modified; a `tmdb` row (vote_average/vote_count) daily as fallback.
* **RISING** = score above the pool floor F (owner.json) with >= 500 votes (TMDB fallback >= 100), non-decreasing over >= 2 successive snapshots (each step >= -0.05). Falling = drop <= -0.3. Write `new-releases/trend.json` (graph id -> rising|falling); the model applies +-0.15.
* **Alerts** (`alerts.tsv`, append-only): alert_date, alert_id, trigger (HIT | RISING | HIT+RISING), title, year, type, service, release_date, hit_types, match_count, imdb_rating, imdb_votes, trend, predicted, on_watchlist, reason, because. Each title alerts once per trigger (`alerts-state.json`); keep `alerts-sent.txt` of what was actually messaged and never resend. `because` names only titles the owner rated, or "you follow X".

## 3. Autoadd (`autoadd_rules.py` = the ONE gate; `autoadd.py` applies it)
A pick may go onto the watchlist (tracker + graph) only if ALL hold: a series (or a movie too if `media` includes movies); predicted >= T; conservative >= T - 0.5; >= 2 independent links to titles rated S+ (the ranking link penalty does not change this); confidence not Low; providers verified (not inferred, not missing); IMDb rating with >= 2,500 votes; owner language; not tracked, seen or skipped; predictions fresh; max 3 adds per run. Default is `--dry-run`. Real adds only if the owner opted in at setup; report every add in one line. Never change these thresholds without the owner's approval.

## 4. Sanity check (`check_new_releases.py`, read-only)
N1 datasets present, readable, < 21 days old (warn > 10). N2 state.json parses; pending file matches it. N3 new-release titles: unique imdb_id/tmdb_id, no seen title is a candidate, providers non-empty, inferred ones flagged, every credited person has nm_id or nm_status. N4 every forward=YES row passes gate_row and has >= 2,500 votes. N5 alerts unique per (title, trigger), on-service and in-language; history well-formed. N6 new-rising rows recent; each picks block of 10 has >= R recent qualifying titles when >= R qualify. N7 no title under 5,000 votes sits at a hard IMDb ceiling; early titles flagged.

skills.name: showrunner-tracker-and-logging
skills.description: Use when the owner rates something, changes a show's status, adds or back-burners a title, asks what to watch next or why a pick was chosen, or when building the tracker CLI, fact logger and seen filter.
skills.content:
---
name: showrunner-tracker-and-logging
description: >-
  Use when the owner rates something, changes a show's status, adds or
  back-burners a title, asks what to watch next or why a pick was chosen, or
  when building the tracker CLI, fact logger and seen filter.
---
# Showrunner: tracker, logging, seen filter, replies (BUILD SPEC + conventions)

## 1. Tracker (`$SR/tracker/tracker.json`, single source of truth for statuses)
`{"shows": {"<tvmaze_id>": {"title", "premiered": "YYYY", "tvmaze_id", "status": "watching|watchlist|watched|dropped", "show_status" (TVmaze: Running/Ended/To Be Determined/In Development), "added": "YYYY-MM-DD", "last_alerted_episode": "S2E5"|null}}}`. Write with `indent=2, sort_keys=True`; never rebuild it from memory.
CLI `$SR/tools/tv.py` (stdlib only, TVmaze `https://api.tvmaze.com`, User-Agent set, 30 s timeout):
* `add <status> <title>`: `/singlesearch/shows?q=`; keeps an existing `added`; prints "Title (year) -> status"; "NOT FOUND" otherwise.
* `set <status> <title>`: substring match on tracked titles, else add.
* `list`: grouped WATCHING / WATCHLIST / WATCHED / DROPPED.
* `check [days=14]`: for every non-dropped show `/shows/<id>?embed[]=nextepisode&embed[]=previousepisode`; JSON with `upcoming` (next episode within days), `returning_soon` (episode 1 of a season within days + 60), `new_aired` (aired in the last 7 days and != last_alerted_episode; then record it), `unknown_date` (TBD/In Development, or Running with no next episode). Refresh `show_status`.
Statuses: watching = most prominent alerts; watchlist = alert on new seasons; watched = alert when a new season is announced or returns; dropped = ignore.
Back burner: "not now, maybe later". Graph `BACK_BURNER{note, added}` + `tracker/back-burner.md` (title, date, note). Back-burnered titles are excluded from picks until the owner revives them.

## 2. Fact logger (`$SR/add_fact`, wrapper runs ensure_up first)
`rate "Title" 8 [--year --type --new]` | `status "Title" watching|watchlist|watched|dropped [--note]` | `watchlist` | `watched` | `backburner "Title" ["note"]` | `follow "Person" [--nm nm...]` | `interest "Genre"` | `like|dislike "Trait or Title" [--note]` | `show "Title"`.
Titles match by exact id/title, then a unique case-insensitive substring; ambiguous or unknown titles need the year (then `--new`, filled from the IMDb dataset by year + type). Every fact is MERGEd and appended to `facts.jsonl` (replayed after a rebuild). Ratings accept halves (7.5).

## 3. Logging conventions
* "I watched X, 8" -> `add_fact rate`, `tv.py set watched` (series), `./predict_all`, then one line: "Logged X: 8. Your top picks moved: ..." (only if the top 10 changed).
* "Loved it" without a number: ask once for a number; if they decline, store their top rating T (model spec) with `inferred:true` (never cited as a link).
* Started / finished / dropped / maybe later -> status or backburner; confirm in one line.
* Same-name remakes: ask for the year before writing anything.
* A rating far from the prediction (|diff| >= 1.5): note it in one line; it feeds the next backtest.

## 4. Seen / exclusion filter (`seen_filter.py`, one definition used everywhere)
Seen = tracker watched/watching/dropped; ratings export; graph RATED, WATCHED, STATUS, DISLIKES, BACK_BURNER; `back-burner.md`; `movies-seen.md`; `exclude-from-predictions.tsv` (known skips; a row ending in `*` excludes a whole franchise family by title prefix). Match by IMDb id first, else normalised title (lower-case, & -> and, punctuation -> space, leading "the" dropped, brand possessive prefixes dropped) plus year when both are known. Applied to candidates before scoring, to discovery, to alerts and to autoadd; QA S2 requires zero leaks across the whole pool.
Namesakes: same title + year with different IMDb ids are kept apart and listed in `known-namesakes.tsv`; never merge them. A true duplicate (same IMDb id) is merged into one node after a JSON backup. People: match by nm_id; same name with a different nm_id gets its own `p:slug-nm...` id; "A and B" duo credits are split; companies get `kind` and are excluded; people without nm_id carry an `nm_status` reason.

## 5. Recommendation reply format
Lead with the answer. Default list = `predictions-picks.tsv` top 10, following `media` in owner.json (series, movies or a mix). One line per pick:
`1. <Title> (<year>) - <predicted, 1 decimal>, <confidence> - <service> - because <one because-line>`
Rules:
* because-lines name only titles the owner actually rated (with the rating) or people they follow; never invent a link. Example: "the writer of <a title they rated> (you gave it <their score>) created this".
* Mark New & Rising slots with "new"; FOLLOW-ON titles say "watch <parent> first"; PROVIDER-INFERRED says "service expected".
* Confidence labels: High = solid public score + 2-3 independent links from their own ratings; Medium = good fit, thinner or mixed evidence; Low = mostly public score or a genre mix they usually rate lower. Never call a prediction a guarantee.
* "Why X?" -> predicted vs conservative score, the links, the main reasons (anchor, people, rules), any caps or flags, in 4-6 short lines.
* "Why not X?" -> its rank and the one or two things holding it back (no links, disliked pair, dated, not on their services, already seen).
* Times in the owner's timezone with a short label. Ask at most one question per reply.
